rv.q: The rituals of community are beautifully portrayed, from candle-lit chiaroscuro tableaux that look like Caravaggio portraits to set pieces of raucous merriment.
Lovers of Fiddler on the Roof will surely enjoy this fresh take on the endearing classic.

Quirks aside, there is love and talent in this Fiddler on the Roof , and even though individual songs might have received patchy applause, the opening-night audience quickly offered a standing ovation.
Director Jordan Fein and resident director Gary Abrahams orchestrate a magnificent, exultant, deeply affecting revitalisation of Fiddler on the Roof.
This new production of Fiddler on the Roof is stunning – visually, aurally and emotionally.
This production balances humour and a rich musical score with the tragedy of a community uprooted from everything it has known.
Fiddler on the Roof is a show with a lot of heart, wonderful music and some innovative touches that enhance the overall performance.

cn.t: Critics praise this triumphant revival as timeless and emotionally resonant, with Troy Sussman's virtuoso performance as Tevye and next-level choreography earning widespread acclaim.
